RESUMO




Os

microrganismos

multirresistentes

(MDR)

representam

uma

das

principais

ameaças

globais

à

saúde

pública

na

atualidade.

Dentre

eles,

destacam-se

os

bacilos

Gram-negativos

resistentes

aos

carbapenêmicos

(BGN-RC),

classificados

pela

Organização

Mundial

da

Saúde

(OMS)

como

prioridade

máxima

para

pesquisa

e

desenvolvimento

de

novos

antibióticos.

A

disseminação

desses

microrganismos

pode

resultar

em

surtos

hospitalares,

nos

quais

a

rápida

identificação

do

patógeno,

a

caracterização

do

perfil

de

resistência

e

a

determinação

das

rotas

de

transmissão

são

essenciais

para

o

manejo

adequado

dos

pacientes,

bem

como

para

a

escolha

de

terapias

antimicrobianas

eficazes.

Este

estudo

teve

como

objetivo

avaliar

a

prevalência

de

carbapenemases

em

BGN-RC

no

Hospital

de

Clínicas

de

Porto

Alegre,

realizar

a

caracterização

molecular

dos

isolados

e

analisar

o

perfil

de

suscetibilidade

a

novos

antimicrobianos,

incluindo

cefiderocol,

meropenem-vaborbactam,

sulbactam-durlobactam

e

ceftazidima-avibactam.

Foi

possível

caracterizar

um

surto

de

Acinetobacter

multirresistente

por

meio

de

análises

genômicas,

identificar

os

genes

de

resistência

aos

carbapenêmicos

mais

prevalentes

em

isolados

de

Pseudomonas

aeruginosa

e

padronizar

a

técnica

de

espectroscopia

no

infravermelho

por

transformada

de

Fourier

(FTIR)

para

a

avaliação

clonal

de

isolados

de

Klebsiella

pneumoniae
.

Além

disso,

foi

avaliado

o

desempenho

da

técnica

de

disco-difusão

em

comparação

à

microdiluição

em

caldo

para

o

teste

de

suscetibilidade

ao

cefiderocol,

bem

como

a

atividade

in

vitro

dos

novos

antimicrobianos

frente

aos

BGN-RC

isolados

de

amostras

clínicas

de

pacientes

atendidos

no

hospital

no

ano

de

2023.

A

caracterização

molecular

dos

isolados

incluiu

a

detecção

de

genes

de

carbapenemases,

análise

fenotípica

por

FTIR

e

análise

genotípica

por

sequenciamento

de

nova

geração,

permitindo

a

avaliação

da

distribuição

clonal

desses

microrganismos.

ABSTRACT




Multidrug-resistant

(MDR)

microorganisms

represent

one

of

the

major

global

public

health

threats

worldwide.

Among

them,

carbapenem-resistant

Gram-negative

bacilli

(CR-GNB)

are

of

particular

concern

and

are

classified

by

the

World

Health

Organization

(WHO)

as

the

highest

priority

for

research

and

development

of

new

antibiotics.

The

spread

of

these

pathogens

may

lead

to

hospital

outbreaks,

in

which

rapid

pathogen

identification,

resistance

profiling,

and

determination

of

transmission

routes

are

essential

for

appropriate

patient

management

and

for

guiding

effective

antimicrobial

therapy.

This

study

aimed

to

assess

the

prevalence

of

CR-GNB

at

the

Hospital

de

Clínicas

de

Porto

Alegre,

to

perform

molecular

characterization

of

the

isolates,

and

to

evaluate

the

susceptibility

profile

to

new

antimicrobials,

including

cefiderocol,

meropenem–vaborbactam,

sulbactam–durlobactam,

and

ceftazidime–avibactam.


A

multidrug-resistant

Acinetobacter

outbreak

was

characterized

through

genomic

analyses,

the

most

prevalent

carbapenem

resistance

genes

among

Pseudomonas

aeruginosa

isolates

were

identified,

and

Fourier-transform

infrared

(FTIR)

spectroscopy

was

standardized

for

clonal

assessment

of

Klebsiella

pneumoniae

isolates.

In

addition,

the

performance

of

the

disk

diffusion

method

was

evaluated

in

comparison

with

broth

microdilution

for

cefiderocol

susceptibility

testing,

as

well

as

the

in

vitro

activity

of

new

antimicrobials

against

CR-GNB

isolated

from

clinical

samples

of

patients

attended

at

the

hospital

in

2023.

Molecular

characterization

included

the

detection

of

carbapenemase

genes,

phenotypic

analysis

by

FTIR

and

genotypic

analysis

by

next-generation

sequencing,

enabling

the

assessment

of

the

clonal

distribution

of

these

microorganisms.

Biotyper;

desse

2024).

os

Carbapenem-resistant

Pseudomonas

aeruginosa

(CRPA)

is

considered

as

one

of

the

high

priority

pathogens

by

the

World

Health

Organization.

As

CRPA

carbapenemase

producers

have

increased

worldwide,

the

aim

of

this

study

was

to

evaluate

the

carbapenemase

prevalence

in

CRPA

at

a

tertiary

care

hospital

in

Brazil”
.

All

395

CRPA

identified

in

the

period

of

September

2021

to

May

2024

were

evaluated

by

multiplex

real-time

polymerase

chain

reaction

(qPCR-HRM)

for

the

following

carbapenemase

genes:

bla
KPC
,

bla
NDM
,

bla
OXA-48-like
,

bla
IMP
,

bla
VIM,

bla
SPM

and

bla
GES
.

In

the

first

period

analyzed

(September

to

December

2021),

almost

70%

of

the

isolates

were

negative

for

the

7

tested

genes,

and

the

bla
NDM

was

found

in

27.3%

of

the

CRPA.

In

the

following

semesters

there

was

an

increase

of

bla
NDM

as

follows:

January

to

June

of

2022

=

29.8%;

July

to

December

of

2022

=

43.8%;

January

to

June

of

2023

=

42.4%;

July

to

December

2023

=

58,9%

and

January

to

May

of

2024

=

59.5%

of

bla
NDM
.

The

prevalence

of

the

other

carbapenemases

remained

low.

an

important

increase

of

bla
NDM

overcoming

the

non-carbapenemase

producers

in

institution.

Pseudomonas

aeruginosa
;

43

Pseudomonas

aeruginosa

is

a

non-fermenting

gram-negative

bacilli

typically

found

in

healthcare

settings,

usually

associated

with

urinary

tract,

respiratory

and

bloodstream

infections.

[1]

Carbapenem-resistant

P.

aeruginosa

(CRPA)

is

particularly

worrying

and

is

considered

a

high-priority

pathogen

in

the

2024

Bacterial

Priority

Pathogens

List

due

to

their

global

threat

and

limited

therapeutic

options.

[2]

Furthermore,

CRPA

are

associated

with

worse

morbidity

and

mortality

outcomes

compared

to

susceptible

isolates,

as

well

as

an

important

impact

on

hospitalization

costs.

[3,4]

The

main

mechanisms

which

lead

to

carbapenem

resistance

in

P.

aeruginosa

are:

efflux

pump

overexpression,

overproduction

of

AmpC

beta-lactamase

usually

associated

with

porin

loss

or

inactivation,

and,

more

rarely,

production

of

carbapenemases.

[5]

While

the

most

prevalent

carbapenemase

gene

worldwide

are

bla
VIM

followed

by

bla
GES
,

[6]

bla
NDM

has

been

emerging

in

the

last

years

in

CRPA

from

Europe

[7],

Africa

[8]

and

other

countries.

[9]

Until

2010,

the

bla
SPM

gene

used

to

be

the

most

common

carbapenemase

among

CRPA

in

southern

Brazil.

[10,11]

However,

a

shift

from

bla
SPM

to

other

carbapenemase

genes,

including

bla
NDM
,

was

described

in

the

last

three

years.

[12]

The

increasing

rates

of

bla
NDM

is

highly

alarming,

as

this

gene

is

commonly

associated

with

resistance

to

carbapenems

and

other

antimicrobial

classes

[13,14]

which

limits

treatment

options.

Therefore,

the

aim

of

this

study

was

to

evaluate

carbapenemase

prevalence

in

CRPA

clinical

isolates

from

a

tertiary

care

hospital

in

southern

Brazil.

All

CRPA

(only

one

isolate

per

patient)

identified

at

the

Microbiology

Laboratory

of

Hospital

de

Clínicas

de

Porto

Alegre

during

the

period

of

September

2021

to

May

2024

were

evaluated

for

carbapenemase

genes

by

multiplex

real-time

polymerase

chain

reaction

(qPCR)

using

high-resolution

melting

(HRM)

analysis

for

bla
SPM
,

bla
KPC
,

bla
NDM
,

bla
OXA-48-like
,

bla
IMP
,

bla
VIM

and

bla
GES

as

previously

described.

[15]

DNA

was

extracted

by

thermal

lysis,

and

qPCR

HRM

was

performed

using

QuantStudio

3®

(Thermo

Fisher).

The

identification

of

the

isolates

was

performed

by

matrix-assisted

laser-desorption

ionization

time-of-flight

mass

spectrometry

-

44

MALDI-TOF

MS

(Bruker

Daltonics)

and

resistance

to

carbapenems

was

determined

by

meropenem

disk

diffusion

method.

[16]

In

the

period

of

this

study,

395

CRPA

isolates

of

P.

aeruginosa

were

evaluated.

A

total

of

218

(55,2%)

presented

carbapenemase

genes

by

qPCR

HRM

assays.

In

the

second

semester

of

2021,

when

carbapenemase

evaluation

in

CRPA

initiated,

almost

70%

(38/55)

of

isolates

were

negative

for

the

7

genes

tested,

and

bla
NDM

gene

was

detected

in

27.3%

(15/55).

In

the

following

semesters,

there

was

a

steadily

increasing

of

bla
NDM

as

follows:

January

to

June

of

2022

=

29.8%

(17/57)

of

bla
NDM
,

July

to

December

of

2022

=

43.8%

(21/48);

January

to

June

of

2023

=

42.4%

(28/66);

July

to

December

2023

=

58,9%

(53/90)

and

January

to

May

of

2024

=

59.5%

(47/79)

of

bla
NDM
.

The

prevalence

of

the

other

carbapenemases

remained

constant

(Figure

1).

bla

in

and

for

genes

all

CRPA

in

Until

recently,

bla
VIM

and

bla
IMP

were

the

most

frequently

carbapenemase

found

in

CRPA

worldwide,

bla
SPM

maintaining

regional

spread

in

Brazil.

[18,19]

This

same

picture

was

seen

in

southern

Brazil

and

in

our

institution.

[10,

11]

A

study

conducted

in

Brazil,

between

November

2015

and

August

2016,

evaluated

28

CRPA

in

hospitalized

patients,

and

the

main

mechanism

involved

in

carbapenem

resistance

was

due

mutations

in

genes

altered

expression

levels,

of

carbapenemases

and

bla
NDM

[20]

Another

study,

conducted

by

Kiffer

et.

al.,

the

prevalence

of

in

brazilian

gram

negative

pathogens

from

2015

to

2022.

This

study

demonstrated

a

high

prevalence

of

P.

aeruginosa

bla
SPM

in

2015

(22.5%)

which

decreased

to

around

10%

in

2016-2019

and

to

less

than

5%

in

2020-2022.

Noteworthy,

the

study

of

Kiffer

et

al.,

indicated

that

the

bla
NDM
,

which

was

very

uncommon

before

2020,

presented

a

steady

increase

from

2021

to

2022

(8.8%

and

6.9%,

respectively).

[12]

In

our

study

we

found

a

significant

increase,

from

September

2021

to

May

2024,

in

carbapenemase

in

CRPA,

markedly

due

to

the

bla
NDM

gene.

Conversely,

CRPA

without

carbapenemase

gene

which

accounted

for

around

70%

in

September

2021

decreased

significantly

to

less

than

37%

in

May

2024.

Although

we

did

not

evaluate

efflux

pump

and

porin

expression,

our

results

demonstrate

that

CRPA

in

our

institution

are

mostly

carbapenemase

producers,

mainly

due

to

the

presence

of

the

bla
NDM

gene.

The

data

from

our

study

is

alarming

as

the

treatment

of

CRPA

bla
NDM

would

not

respond

to

the

treatment

with

the

new

beta

lactam/beta

lactamase

combinations

no

activity

against

metallo

enzymes

such

as

NDM.

[21]

Furthermore,

while

bla
SPM

was

usually

carried

in

plasmids

not

associated

with

other

antimicrobial

resistant

genes,

[18]

bla
NDM

was

found

in

plasmids

carrying

genes

that

lead

to

resistance

to

aminoglycosides

and

fluoroquinolones.

[13,14]


46

This

study

reinforces

the

need

for

surveillance

of

and

early

of

CRPA

the

empirical

with

ceftazidime/avibactam

to

improve

resources

against

these

infections.

Background


Acinetobacter

seifertii

is

one

of

the

six

species

belonging

to

the

Acinetobacter

calcoaceticus-baumannii

complex

(
A.

baumannii
,

A.

calcoaceticus
,

A.

nosocomialis
,

A.

pitti
,

A.

lactucae

and

Acinetobacter

genomic

species

“between

1

and

3”).
1

The

first

report

of


A.

seifertii

obtained

from

human

clinical

specimens

occurred

in

2015

in

isolates

from

different

countries.
2

Recent

reports

suggested

a

higher

incidence

of

shock

and

high

Pitt

bacteremia

score

associated

with

A.

seifertti

compared

to

A.

baumannii

infections
3
.

Despite

its

prevalence

is

not

well-established,

A.

seifertti

seems

to

be

an

emerging

pathogen

associated

with

severe

infections,

mainly

in

the

elderly

and

children.
4

Carbapenem-resistant

A.

baumannii

(CRAB)

outbreaks

have

been

documented

in

various

hospital

settings,

including

Intensive

Care

Units

(ICUs),

emergency

departments,

and

general

wards.

These

outbreaks

often

involve

multiple

patients

and

can

be

challenging

due

to

CRAB

survival

ability

on

dry

surfaces

and

their

resistance

to

common

disinfectants.
5,6

The

resistance

to

carbapenems

is

often

due

to

carbapenemase

genes

such

as

bla
OXA-23
,

bla
IMP,

and

bla
NDM

which

are

usually

localized

in

plasmids

and

eventually

integrated

into

the

bacterial

chromosome.

Although

there

are

few

reports

of

outbreaks

caused

by

A.

seifertti
,

the

resistance

and

virulence

mechanisms

appear

to

be

similar

to

other

species

from

the

A.

baumannii-calcoaceticus

complex.
4

Furthermore,

it

is

capable

to

transfer

carbapenem-resistant

determinants

to

other

species

of

A.

baumannii

complex

which

highlights

the

importance

of

monitoring

its

emergence
7
.

Antimicrobial

resistance

is

considered

one

of

the

top

ten

global

public

health

threats

to

humanity,
8

and

CRAB

complex

was

identified

as

a

critical-priority

pathogen

by

the

World

Health

Organization

(WHO)
9

since

the

treatment

poses

as

a

considerable

challenge.
10

In

this

context,

this

study

aimed

to

investigate

an

outbreak

of

carbapenem-resistant

A.

seifertii

(CRAS)

among

neonates

admitted

to

the

Neonatal

Intensive

Care

Unit

(NICU)

at

a

hospital

in

southern

Brazil.


51

Material

and

Methods



Outbreak

Investigation


This

study

was

conducted

at

“Hospital

de

Clínicas

de

Porto

Alegre”

located

in

southern

Brazil,

an

860-bed

tertiary

care

university

hospital

with

a

20-bed

NICU.

The

first

case

of

CRAS

was

identified

in

June

2023

in

sputum

and

blood

culture

specimens

collected

from

a

newborn

hospitalized

for

50

days.

The

second

and

third

cases

were

identified

in

July

2023,

characterizing

the

onset

of

the

outbreak.



Proactive

Implementation

of

Infection

Control

Measures


A

set

of

additional

measures

were

implemented

by

the

Infection

Control

Service

in

response

to

the

identification

of

the

three

first

CRAS

cases.

These

measures

included

contact

screening

conducted

through

swabs

for

culture

surveillance;

the

isolation

of

all

patients

in

cohorting

beds

with

stringent

contact

precaution

measures;

limited

access

to

NICU

restricting

for

one

partner

and

exclusive

staff.

Further,

specific

guidance

was

provided

to

parents

on

appropriate

conduct

during

hospitalization

and

after

discharge,

emphasizing

the

importance

of

avoiding

unnecessary

movement

within

the

unit,

avoiding

contact

with

other

parents

and

patients,

and

maintaining

strict

hand

hygiene.


52

Additionally,

the

standard

protocols

were

revised

and

a

total

of

142

staff

members

were

trained

to

reinforce

contact

precautions

procedures

which

included

hand

hygiene,

the

proper

use

of

gloves

and

gowns,

disinfection

of

surfaces

around

the

bed

three

times

a

day,

and

the

exclusive

use

of

medical

devices,

which

were

disinfected

after

each

use.

Terminal

cleaning

of

beds

was

performed

after

patients

were

discarded.

Proper

storage

of

isolates

identified

by

the

microbiology

laboratory

was

ensured.

The

health

surveillance

authority

was

immediately

notified

of

the

outbreak

to

allow

for

a

coordinated

and

effective

response.



Microbiological

Methods


Species

were

identified

using

matrix-assisted

laser

desorption

ionization

time-of-flight

mass

spectrometry

(MALDI-TOF

MS)

with

the

VITEK

MS®

v3.0

database

(bioMérieux,

Marcy

l'Etoile,

France).

Meropenem

resistance

was

determined

by

disk

diffusion,

and

antimicrobial

susceptibility

to

trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole,

ciprofloxacin,

gentamicin,

amikacin,

and

ampicillin/sulbactam

was

performed

using

the

Sensititre

system

(Thermo

Fisher

Scientific,

Waltham,

MA,

USA),

with

GNX3F

and

MDR2GNXXF

plates.

The

antimicrobial

susceptibility

interpretation

was

performed

according

to

the

EUCAST

guidelines,

except

for

ampicillin/sulbactam,

which

was

according

to

the

CLSI

guidelines.

In

addition,

the

minimal

inhibitory

concentration

(MIC)

for

polymyxin

B

was

determined

by

standard

broth

microdilution

(BMD),

according

to

the

EUCAST

guidelines.

68

Introduction


Carbapenem-resistant

Klebsiella

pneumoniae

(CRKP)

is

one

of

the

top

priority

pathogens

of

concern

in

public

health

(WHO,

2024).

Therefore,

it

is

important

to

develop

methodologies

to

track

in

real

time

the

spread

in

healthcare

settings

of

the

CRKP

strains

with

high

potential

to

cause

outbreaks

of

infection

due

to

increased

antibiotic

resistance

and/or

with

virulence

factors.

(Gomez-Simmonds,

2017;

Holt,

2015).

Bacterial

typing

is

commonly

performed

for

monitoring

and

characterization

of

bacterial

isolates

by

using

genetic

methods,

which

can

determine

capsular

type

according

to

K

locus

(KL),

strain

type

(ST),

core

genome

multilocus

sequence

typing

(cgMLST)

and

other

features

(Podschun

&

Ullman,

1998;

Simar,

2021).

These

methods,

which

demand

sequencing

of

some

genes

or

the

whole

genome,

are

expensive,

laborious

and

time-consuming.

As

an

alternative,

Fourier-transform

infrared

(FTIR)

spectroscopy

has

emerged

as

a

tool

for

typing

(Dinkelacker,

2018;

Martak,

2019).

FTIR

spectroscopy

is

a

phenotypic

method

based

on

differential

vibration

of

distinct

chemical

bonds

of

the

molecules

present

in

the

bacterial

cell

by

exposure

to

an

infrared

beam.

As

distinct

functional

chemical

groups

absorb

infrared

radiation

at

different

wavelengths,

specific

spectral

peaks

are

generated

which

are

related

to

the

absorbance

to

wavenumbers

(Novais,

2019).

This

methodology

has

been

applied

to

evaluate

the

relationship

among

isolates

in

an

outbreak

(Uribe,

2023;

Teng,

2022;

Rakovitsky,

2020)

and

to

classify

bacteria

according

to

a

specific

feature,

such

as

the

KL

type

(Rodrigues,

2020;

Novais,

2024),

which

can

be

used

for

bacterial

characterization

and

surveillance.

The

KL

is

a

chromosomal

region

that

encodes

approximately

10

to

30

genes

responsible

for

the

capsule

biosynthesis

pathway.

To

date,

there

are

a

total

of

147

loci

defined,

and

the

KL

types

were

found

to

be

very

related

to

the

serologically

defined

K

type

(capsule

antigen)

(Lam,

2022).

Although

studies

evaluating

KL

typing

by

FTIR

have

employed

the

mode

of

attenuated

total

reflectance

(ATR)

presented

promising

results

(Rodrigues,

2020;

Novais,

2024),

studies

assessing

the

transmission

mode

are

still

lacking.

69

IR

Biotyper

is

a

platform

developed

by

Bruker

(Daltonik,

GmbH),

which

uses

FTIR

in

transmission

mode

and

presents

a

very

user-friendly

software.

It

allows

the

users

to

evaluate

the

relatedness

of

bacterial

isolates

in

only

a

few

minutes

and

to

classify

them

according

to

some

features

with

the

application

of

artificial

intelligence

to

develop

a

classifier

(Martak,

2019;

Burckhardt,

2019).

Therefore,

the

aim

of

this

study

was

to

develop

a

classifier

and

evaluate

the

capability

of

IR

Biotyper

in

classifying

bacterial

isolates

according

to

KL

type.

The

study

also

evaluated

the

performance

of

IR

Biotyper

for

typing

K.

pneumoniae

according

to

the

ST.

Discussion



FTIR

is

a

phenotypic

method

traditionally

used

in

chemistry

to

determine

the

molecular

composition

of

a

wide

variety

of

structures

in

a

rapid,

non-destructive,

simple,

cheap

and

high-throughput

manner.

FTIR

has

also

evolved

for

bacterial

identification

(Maccannell,

2013).

The

IR

Biotyper

equipment

(Bruker

Daltonik,

76

GmbH),

available

since

2018,

is

a

system

based

on

the

FTIR

technology,

which

allows

rapid

bacterial

molecular

typing

(Novais,

2019).

Until

recently,

a

few

studies

have

evaluated

the

capability

of

IR

Biotyper

to

characterize

isolates

compared

to

WGS

(Uribe,

2023;

Kon,

2024;

Scheier,

2023;

Passaris,

2022).

Considering

K.

pneumoniae

isolates,

recent

studies

have

indicated

that

the

IR

Biotyper

did

not

present

reliable

results

to

classify

isolates

in

the

same

cluster

of

ST.

In

fact,

the

results

demonstrated

that

the

IR

Biotyper

grouped

in

the

same

cluster

isolates

of

different

STs

(Candela,

2025)

or

did

not

group

all

the

same

STs

within

the

same

clusters

(Hu,

2021).

We

also

found

similar

results

when

considering

the

results

of

IR

Biotyper

in

comparison

to

the

STs

established

by

WGS.

K.

pneumoniae

is

known

to

have

mucoid

appearance

in

culture

media

due

to

well-developed

capsules,

which

are

divided

into

77

types.

Also,

capsule

typing

demonstrated

to

be

a

good

marker

for

serotyping

with

good

reproducibility

and

capability

to

differentiate

clinical

isolates

(Podschun

&

Ullman,

1998;

Orskov,

1984).

Additionally,

approximately

all

capsule

serotypes

are

correlated

to

the

KL

(Lam,

2022).

We,

therefore,

attempted

to

evaluate

the

capability

of

IR

Biotyper

to

type

K.

pneumoniae

according

to

the

ST

as

well

as

KL.

As

mentioned

before,

considering

only

the

ST,

the

IR

Biotyper

presented

a

low

correlation

with

WGS,

as

isolates

belonging

to

the

same

ST

were

distributed

in

different

clusters

as

well

as

different

STs

were

grouped

into

the

same

cluster

(Figure

2).

When

we

use

KL

to

evaluate

K.

pneumoniae
,

all

73

isolates

were

grouped

according

to

their

KL

type

(Figure

1

and

Figure

3),

indicating

that

FT-IR

correlates

well

with

KL

for

typing

K.

pneumoniae

isolates

using

the

IR

Biotyper.

However,

it

is

important

to

notice

that

this

study

did

not

include

multiple

STs

sharing

the

same

KL,

which

would

allow

direct

comparison

of

KL

clustering

across

different

genetic

backgrounds.

Therefore,

it

remains

unconfirmed

whether

FT-IR

typing

by

KL

would

always

distinguish

unrelated

STs

with

the

same

KL

and

future

studies

are

needed

to

address

these

complementary

genomic

approaches.

Furthermore,

we

created

a

classifier

using

54

isolates

correctly

separated

by

the

KL,

in

order

to

classify

the

remaining

isolates.

When

the

classification

was

performed,

15

isolates

were

correctly

classified

according

to

their

KL,

whereas

only

77

the

isolates

with

KL15,

KL10

and

KL46

(not

included

in

the

classifier

training

set)

were

wrongly

classified

as

KL

102.

Nevertheless,

the

score

of

this

classification

-

the

confidence

value

(0–100%)

generated

by

the

classifier

when

assigning

a

KL

type

-

was

0%

(Table

1),

which

indicates

that

there

is

no

reliability

in

this

classification,

as

expected.

Interestingly,

1

isolate

(GKPN

0375),

which

was

correctly

classified

into

its

KL,

showed

a

0%

score,

indicating

that

the

classifier

may

be

improved,

possibly

considering

a

different

cutoff

or

different

parameters

for

accepting

the

results

of

the

classifier.

Therefore,

more

studies

are

needed

before

considering

the

classifier

for

use

in

a

laboratory

routine.

To

the

best

of

our

knowledge,

this

is

the

first

study

to

use

the

KL

to

type

different

strains

of

K.

pneumoniae

using

the

IR

Biotyper

technology.

Use

of

a

classifier

considering

the

KLs

and

STs

in

the

IR

Biotyper

demonstrated

to

be

a

promising

tool

to

type

K.

pneumoniae

in

a

faster

and

cost-effective

way

compared

to

WGS.

alta

complexidade

da

Sul

do

Brasil,

longo

de

um

período

de

um

ano

(2023).

Esses

achados

contribuem

de

forma

significativa

para

o

entendimento

do

cenário

local

de

resistência

aos

carbapenêmicos

em

um

centro

de

referência,

a

importância

da

vigilância

microbiológica

contínua.

Adicionalmente,

foi

possível

estabelecer

o

perfil

de

suscetibilidade

desses

isolados

frente

a

novos

antimicrobianos

-

cefiderocol,

meropenem–vaborbactam

e

sulbactam–durlobactam

-

ainda

não

disponíveis

para

uso

clínico

no

Brasil.

A

avaliação

da

atividade

in

vitro

desses

agentes

fornece

subsídios

relevantes

para

o

conhecimento

epidemiológico

e

terapêutico,

especialmente

no

contexto

de

uma

futura

incorporação

dessas

opções

no

arsenal

antimicrobiano

nacional.

Paralelamente,

avaliou-se

o

perfil

de

suscetibilidade

in

vitro

à

ceftazidima–avibactam,

antimicrobiano

recentemente

introduzido

na

prática

clínica

brasileira,

ampliando

a

compreensão

sobre

sua

efetividade

frente

a

isolados

multirresistentes.

O

estudo

também

permitiu

a

identificação

de

achados

epidemiológicos

relevantes,

incluindo

o

aumento

da

prevalência

da

enzima

NDM

em

isolados

de

Pseudomonas

aeruginosa

e

a

caracterização

de

um

surto

envolvendo

Acinetobacter

seifertii

pertencente

a

uma

nova

cepa

durante

o

período

avaliado.

Esses

resultados

evidenciam

a

dinâmica

evolutiva

dos

mecanismos

de

resistência

e

ressaltam

o

impacto

clínico

e

epidemiológico

de

clones

emergentes

em

ambientes

hospitalares.

No

que

tange

a

comparação

entre

os

métodos

de

disco-difusão

e

microdiluição

em

caldo

para

a

determinação

da

suscetibilidade

ao

cefiderocol,

foi

possível

determinar

discrepâncias

significativas

entre

as

técnicas.

achados

reforçam

a

necessidade

de

cautela

por

parte

dos

laboratórios

de

microbiologia

clínica

na

interpretação

dos

resultados

obtidos

por

como

97

sugerem

a

importância

de

revisões

críticas

dos

de

corte

clínicos

atualmente

recomendados

diretrizes

internacionais,

o

antimicrobiano.

avaliação

do

Biotyper,

um

classificador

Os

multirresistentes

(MDR)

representam

uma

eles,

os

bacilos

Gram-negativos

carbapenêmicos

Organização

Mundial

de

novos

disseminação

em

BGN-RC

Hospital

antimicrobianos,

cefiderocol,

meropenem-vaborbactam,

ABSTRACT




Multidrug-resistant

(MDR)

microorganisms

represent

one

of

the

major

global

public

health

threats

worldwide.

Among

them,

carbapenem-resistant

Gram-negative

bacilli

(CR-GNB)

are

of

particular

concern

and

are

classified

by

the

World

Health

Organization

(WHO)

as

the

highest

priority

for

research

and

development

of

new

antibiotics.

The

spread

of

these

pathogens

may

lead

to

hospital

outbreaks,

in

which

rapid

pathogen

identification,

resistance

profiling,

and

determination

of

transmission

routes

are

essential

for

appropriate

patient

management

and

for

guiding

effective

antimicrobial

therapy.

This

study

aimed

to

assess

the

prevalence

of

CR-GNB

at

the

Hospital

de

Clínicas

de

Porto

Alegre,

to

perform

molecular

characterization

of

the

isolates,

and

to

evaluate

the

susceptibility

profile

to

new

antimicrobials,

including

cefiderocol,

meropenem–vaborbactam,

sulbactam–durlobactam,

and

ceftazidime–avibactam.


A

multidrug-resistant

Acinetobacter

outbreak

was

characterized

through

genomic

analyses,

the

most

prevalent

carbapenem

resistance

genes

among

Pseudomonas

aeruginosa

isolates

were

identified,

and

Fourier-transform

infrared

(FTIR)

spectroscopy

was

standardized

for

clonal

assessment

of

Klebsiella

pneumoniae

isolates.

In

addition,

the

performance

of

the

disk

diffusion

method

was

evaluated

in

comparison

with

broth

microdilution

for

cefiderocol

susceptibility

testing,

as

well

as

the

in

vitro

activity

of

new

antimicrobials

against

CR-GNB

isolated

from

clinical

samples

of

patients

attended

at

the

hospital

in

2023.

Molecular

characterization

included

the

detection

of

carbapenemase

genes,

phenotypic

analysis

by

FTIR

and

genotypic

analysis

by

next-generation

sequencing,

enabling

the

assessment

of

the

clonal

distribution

of

these

microorganisms.

Biotyper;

os

by

aim

of

to

the

carbapenemase

prevalence

in

CRPA

at

a

tertiary

care

hospital

in

Brazil”
.

395

CRPA

identified

the

period

of

September

2021

to

May

2024

were

evaluated

by

real-time

polymerase

chain

reaction

(qPCR-HRM)

following

carbapenemase

bla
KPC
,

bla
NDM
,

OXA-48-like
,

bla
IMP
,

bla
VIM,

bla
SPM

and

bla
GES
.

In

period

analyzed

(September

to

December

2021),

70%

of

isolates

negative

for

the

7

the

bla
NDM

in

of

the

CRPA.

In

NDM

January

=

43

Pseudomonas

aeruginosa

is

a

non-fermenting

gram-negative

bacilli

typically

found

in

healthcare

settings,

usually

associated

with

urinary

tract,

respiratory

and

bloodstream

infections.

[1]

Carbapenem-resistant

P.

aeruginosa

(CRPA)

is

particularly

worrying

and

is

considered

a

high-priority

pathogen

in

the

2024

Bacterial

Priority

Pathogens

List

due

to

their

global

threat

and

limited

therapeutic

options.

[2]

Furthermore,

CRPA

are

associated

with

worse

morbidity

and

mortality

outcomes

compared

to

susceptible

isolates,

as

well

as

an

important

impact

on

hospitalization

costs.

[3,4]

The

main

mechanisms

which

lead

to

carbapenem

resistance

in

P.

aeruginosa

are:

efflux

pump

overexpression,

overproduction

of

AmpC

beta-lactamase

usually

associated

with

porin

loss

or

inactivation,

and,

more

rarely,

production

of

carbapenemases.

[5]

While

the

most

prevalent

carbapenemase

gene

worldwide

are

bla
VIM

followed

by

bla
GES
,

[6]

bla
NDM

has

been

emerging

in

the

last

years

in

CRPA

from

Europe

[7],

Africa

[8]

and

other

countries.

[9]

Until

2010,

the

bla
SPM

gene

used

to

be

the

most

common

carbapenemase

among

CRPA

in

southern

Brazil.

[10,11]

However,

a

shift

from

bla
SPM

to

other

carbapenemase

genes,

including

bla
NDM
,

was

described

in

the

last

three

years.

[12]

The

increasing

rates

of

bla
NDM

is

highly

alarming,

as

this

gene

is

commonly

associated

with

resistance

to

carbapenems

and

other

antimicrobial

classes

[13,14]

which

limits

treatment

options.

Therefore,

the

aim

of

this

study

was

to

evaluate

carbapenemase

prevalence

in

CRPA

clinical

isolates

from

a

tertiary

care

hospital

in

southern

Brazil.

All

CRPA

(only

one

isolate

per

patient)

identified

at

the

Microbiology

Laboratory

of

Hospital

de

Clínicas

de

Porto

Alegre

during

the

period

of

September

2021

to

May

2024

were

evaluated

for

carbapenemase

genes

by

multiplex

real-time

polymerase

chain

reaction

(qPCR)

using

high-resolution

melting

(HRM)

analysis

for

bla
SPM
,

bla
KPC
,

bla
NDM
,

bla
OXA-48-like
,

bla
IMP
,

bla
VIM

and

bla
GES

as

previously

described.

[15]

DNA

was

extracted

by

thermal

lysis,

and

qPCR

HRM

was

performed

using

QuantStudio

3®

(Thermo

Fisher).

The

identification

of

the

isolates

was

performed

by

matrix-assisted

laser-desorption

ionization

time-of-flight

mass

spectrometry

-

44

MALDI-TOF

MS

(Bruker

Daltonics)

and

resistance

to

carbapenems

was

determined

by

meropenem

disk

diffusion

method.

[16]

In

the

period

of

this

study,

395

CRPA

isolates

of

P.

aeruginosa

were

evaluated.

A

total

of

218

(55,2%)

presented

carbapenemase

genes

by

qPCR

HRM

assays.

In

the

second

semester

of

2021,

when

carbapenemase

evaluation

in

CRPA

initiated,

almost

70%

(38/55)

of

isolates

were

negative

for

the

7

genes

tested,

and

bla
NDM

gene

was

detected

in

27.3%

(15/55).

In

the

following

semesters,

there

was

a

steadily

increasing

of

bla
NDM

as

follows:

January

to

June

of

2022

=

29.8%

(17/57)

of

bla
NDM
,

July

to

December

of

2022

=

43.8%

(21/48);

January

to

June

of

2023

=

42.4%

(28/66);

July

to

December

2023

=

58,9%

(53/90)

and

January

to

May

of

2024

=

59.5%

(47/79)

of

bla
NDM
.

The

prevalence

of

the

other

carbapenemases

remained

constant

(Figure

1).

all

and

carbapenemase

SPM

in

This

picture

was

in

southern

Brazil

and

in

our

institution.

[10,

11]

A

study

conducted

in

Brazil,

between

November

2015

and

August

2016,

evaluated

28

CRPA

in

hospitalized

patients,

and

the

main

involved

in

NDM

Another

Kiffer

gram

negative

pathogens

to

This

study

high

prevalence

of

P.

aeruginosa

bla
SPM

in

2015

(22.5%)

which

decreased

to

around

10%

in

2016-2019

and

to

less

than

5%

in

2020-2022.

Noteworthy,

the

study

of

Kiffer

et

al.,

indicated

that

the

bla
NDM
,

which

was

very

uncommon

before

2020,

presented

a

steady

increase

from

2021

to

2022

(8.8%

and

6.9%,

respectively).

[12]

In

our

study

we

found

a

significant

increase,

from

September

2021

to

May

2024,

in

carbapenemase

in

CRPA,

markedly

due

to

the

bla
NDM

gene.

Conversely,

CRPA

without

carbapenemase

gene

which

accounted

for

around

70%

in

September

2021

significantly

to

less

than

37%

in

May

2024.

Although

we

did

not

evaluate

efflux

pump

and

porin

expression,

our

results

demonstrate

that

CRPA

in

our

institution

are

mostly

carbapenemase

producers,

mainly

due

to

the

presence

of

the

bla
NDM

gene.

The

data

from

our

study

is

alarming

as

the

treatment

of

CRPA

bla
NDM

beta

lactam/beta

enzymes

NDM.

[21]

Furthermore,

while

bla
SPM

with

other

antimicrobial

resistant

genes,

[18]

NDM

lead

resistance

to

aminoglycosides

and

fluoroquinolones.

[13,14]

This

study

reinforces

the

Background


Acinetobacter

seifertii

is

one

of

the

six

species

belonging

to

the

Acinetobacter

calcoaceticus-baumannii

complex

(
A.

baumannii
,

A.

calcoaceticus
,

A.

nosocomialis
,

A.

pitti
,

A.

lactucae

and

Acinetobacter

genomic

species

“between

1

and

3”).
1

The

first

report

of


A.

seifertii

obtained

from

human

clinical

specimens

occurred

in

2015

in

isolates

from

different

countries.
2

Recent

reports

suggested

a

higher

incidence

of

shock

and

high

Pitt

bacteremia

score

associated

with

A.

seifertti

compared

to

A.

baumannii

infections
3
.

Despite

its

prevalence

is

not

well-established,

A.

seifertti

seems

to

be

an

emerging

pathogen

associated

with

severe

infections,

mainly

in

the

elderly

and

children.
4

Carbapenem-resistant

A.

baumannii

(CRAB)

outbreaks

have

been

documented

in

various

hospital

settings,

including

Intensive

Care

Units

(ICUs),

emergency

departments,

and

general

wards.

These

outbreaks

often

involve

multiple

patients

and

can

be

challenging

due

to

CRAB

survival

ability

on

dry

surfaces

and

their

resistance

to

common

disinfectants.
5,6

The

resistance

to

carbapenems

is

often

due

to

carbapenemase

genes

such

as

bla
OXA-23
,

bla
IMP,

and

bla
NDM

which

are

usually

localized

in

plasmids

and

eventually

integrated

into

the

bacterial

chromosome.

Although

there

are

few

reports

of

outbreaks

caused

by

A.

seifertti
,

the

resistance

and

virulence

mechanisms

appear

to

be

similar

to

other

species

from

the

A.

baumannii-calcoaceticus

complex.
4

Furthermore,

it

is

capable

to

transfer

carbapenem-resistant

determinants

to

other

species

of

A.

baumannii

complex

which

highlights

the

importance

of

monitoring

its

emergence
7
.

Antimicrobial

resistance

is

considered

one

of

the

top

ten

global

public

health

threats

to

humanity,
8

and

CRAB

complex

was

identified

as

a

critical-priority

pathogen

by

the

World

Health

Organization

(WHO)
9

since

the

treatment

poses

as

a

considerable

challenge.
10

In

this

context,

this

study

aimed

to

investigate

an

outbreak

of

carbapenem-resistant

A.

seifertii

(CRAS)

among

neonates

admitted

to

the

Neonatal

Intensive

Care

Unit

(NICU)

at

a

hospital

in

southern

Brazil.


51

Material

and

Methods



Outbreak

Investigation


This

study

was

conducted

at

“Hospital

de

Clínicas

de

Porto

Alegre”

located

in

southern

Brazil,

an

860-bed

tertiary

care

university

hospital

with

a

20-bed

NICU.

The

first

case

of

CRAS

was

identified

in

June

2023

in

sputum

and

blood

culture

specimens

collected

from

a

newborn

hospitalized

for

50

days.

The

second

and

third

cases

were

identified

in

July

2023,

characterizing

the

onset

of

the

outbreak.



Proactive

Implementation

of

Infection

Control

Measures


A

set

of

additional

measures

were

implemented

by

the

Infection

Control

Service

in

response

to

the

identification

of

the

three

first

CRAS

cases.

These

measures

included

contact

screening

conducted

through

swabs

for

culture

surveillance;

the

isolation

of

all

patients

in

cohorting

beds

with

stringent

contact

precaution

measures;

limited

access

to

NICU

restricting

for

one

partner

and

exclusive

staff.

Further,

specific

guidance

was

provided

to

parents

on

appropriate

conduct

during

hospitalization

and

after

discharge,

emphasizing

the

importance

of

avoiding

unnecessary

movement

within

the

unit,

avoiding

contact

with

other

parents

and

patients,

and

maintaining

strict

hand

hygiene.


52

Additionally,

the

standard

protocols

were

revised

and

a

total

of

142

staff

members

were

trained

to

reinforce

contact

precautions

procedures

which

included

hand

hygiene,

the

proper

use

of

gloves

and

gowns,

disinfection

of

surfaces

around

the

bed

three

times

a

day,

and

the

exclusive

use

of

medical

devices,

which

were

disinfected

after

each

use.

Terminal

cleaning

of

beds

was

performed

after

patients

were

discarded.

Proper

storage

of

isolates

identified

by

the

microbiology

laboratory

was

ensured.

The

health

surveillance

authority

was

immediately

notified

of

the

outbreak

to

allow

for

a

coordinated

and

effective

response.



Microbiological

Methods


Species

were

identified

using

matrix-assisted

laser

desorption

ionization

time-of-flight

mass

spectrometry

(MALDI-TOF

MS)

with

the

VITEK

MS®

v3.0

database

(bioMérieux,

Marcy

l'Etoile,

France).

Meropenem

resistance

was

determined

by

disk

diffusion,

and

antimicrobial

susceptibility

to

trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole,

ciprofloxacin,

gentamicin,

amikacin,

and

ampicillin/sulbactam

was

performed

using

the

Sensititre

system

(Thermo

Fisher

Scientific,

Waltham,

MA,

USA),

with

GNX3F

and

MDR2GNXXF

plates.

The

antimicrobial

susceptibility

interpretation

was

performed

according

to

the

EUCAST

guidelines,

except

for

ampicillin/sulbactam,

which

was

according

to

the

CLSI

guidelines.

In

addition,

the

minimal

inhibitory

concentration

(MIC)

for

polymyxin

B

was

determined

by

standard

broth

microdilution

(BMD),

according

to

the

EUCAST

guidelines.

Holt,

2015).

Bacterial

typing

is

commonly

performed

for

monitoring

and

characterization

of

bacterial

isolates

by

using

genetic

methods,

which

can

determine

capsular

type

according

to

K

locus

(KL),

strain

type

(ST),

core

genome

multilocus

sequence

typing

(cgMLST)

and

other

features

(Podschun

&

Ullman,

1998;

Simar,

2021).

These

methods,

which

demand

sequencing

of

some

genes

or

the

whole

genome,

are

expensive,

laborious

and

time-consuming.

As

an

alternative,

Fourier-transform

infrared

(FTIR)

spectroscopy

has

emerged

as

a

tool

for

typing

(Dinkelacker,

2018;

Martak,

2019).

FTIR

spectroscopy

is

a

phenotypic

method

based

on

differential

vibration

of

distinct

chemical

bonds

of

the

molecules

present

in

the

bacterial

cell

by

exposure

to

an

infrared

beam.

As

distinct

functional

chemical

groups

absorb

infrared

radiation

at

different

wavelengths,

specific

spectral

peaks

are

generated

which

are

related

to

the

absorbance

to

wavenumbers

(Novais,

2019).

This

methodology

has

been

applied

to

evaluate

the

relationship

among

isolates

in

an

outbreak

(Uribe,

2023;

Teng,

2022;

Rakovitsky,

2020)

and

to

classify

bacteria

according

to

a

specific

feature,

such

as

the

KL

type

(Rodrigues,

2020;

Novais,

2024),

which

can

be

used

for

bacterial

characterization

and

surveillance.

The

KL

is

a

chromosomal

region

that

encodes

approximately

10

to

30

genes

responsible

for

the

capsule

biosynthesis

pathway.

To

date,

there

are

a

total

of

147

loci

defined,

and

the

KL

types

were

found

to

be

very

related

to

the

serologically

defined

K

type

(capsule

antigen)

(Lam,

2022).

Although

studies

evaluating

KL

typing

by

FTIR

have

employed

the

mode

of

attenuated

total

reflectance

(ATR)

presented

promising

results

(Rodrigues,

2020;

Novais,

2024),

studies

assessing

the

transmission

mode

are

still

lacking.

69

IR

Biotyper

is

a

platform

developed

by

Bruker

(Daltonik,

GmbH),

which

uses

FTIR

in

transmission

mode

and

presents

a

very

user-friendly

software.

It

allows

the

users

to

evaluate

the

relatedness

of

bacterial

isolates

in

only

a

few

minutes

and

to

classify

them

according

to

some

features

with

the

application

of

artificial

intelligence

to

develop

a

classifier

(Martak,

2019;

Burckhardt,

2019).

Therefore,

the

aim

of

this

study

was

to

develop

a

classifier

and

evaluate

the

capability

of

IR

Biotyper

in

classifying

bacterial

isolates

according

to

KL

type.

The

study

also

evaluated

the

performance

of

IR

Biotyper

for

typing

K.

pneumoniae

according

to

the

ST.

Discussion



FTIR

is

a

phenotypic

method

traditionally

used

in

chemistry

to

determine

the

molecular

composition

of

a

wide

variety

of

structures

in

a

rapid,

non-destructive,

simple,

cheap

and

high-throughput

manner.

FTIR

has

also

evolved

for

bacterial

identification

(Maccannell,

2013).

The

IR

Biotyper

equipment

(Bruker

Daltonik,

76

GmbH),

available

since

2018,

is

a

system

based

on

the

FTIR

technology,

which

allows

rapid

bacterial

molecular

typing

(Novais,

2019).

Until

recently,

a

few

studies

have

evaluated

the

capability

of

IR

Biotyper

to

characterize

isolates

compared

to

WGS

(Uribe,

2023;

Kon,

2024;

Scheier,

2023;

Passaris,

2022).

Considering

K.

pneumoniae

isolates,

recent

studies

have

indicated

that

the

IR

Biotyper

did

not

present

reliable

results

to

classify

isolates

in

the

same

cluster

of

ST.

In

fact,

the

results

demonstrated

that

the

IR

Biotyper

grouped

in

the

same

cluster

isolates

of

different

STs

(Candela,

2025)

or

did

not

group

all

the

same

STs

within

the

same

clusters

(Hu,

2021).

We

also

found

similar

results

when

considering

the

results

of

IR

Biotyper

in

comparison

to

the

STs

established

by

WGS.

K.

pneumoniae

is

known

to

have

mucoid

appearance

in

culture

media

due

to

well-developed

capsules,

which

are

divided

into

77

types.

Also,

capsule

typing

demonstrated

to

be

a

good

marker

for

serotyping

with

good

reproducibility

and

capability

to

differentiate

clinical

isolates

(Podschun

&

Ullman,

1998;

Orskov,

1984).

Additionally,

approximately

all

capsule

serotypes

are

correlated

to

the

KL

(Lam,

2022).

We,

therefore,

attempted

to

evaluate

the

capability

of

IR

Biotyper

to

type

K.

pneumoniae

according

to

the

ST

as

well

as

KL.

As

mentioned

before,

considering

only

the

ST,

the

IR

Biotyper

presented

a

low

correlation

with

WGS,

as

isolates

belonging

to

the

same

ST

were

distributed

in

different

clusters

as

well

as

different

STs

were

grouped

into

the

same

cluster

(Figure

2).

When

we

use

KL

to

evaluate

K.

pneumoniae
,

all

73

isolates

were

grouped

according

to

their

KL

type

(Figure

1

and

Figure

3),

indicating

that

FT-IR

correlates

well

with

KL

for

typing

K.

pneumoniae

isolates

using

the

IR

Biotyper.

However,

it

is

important

to

notice

that

this

study

did

not

include

multiple

STs

sharing

the

same

KL,

which

would

allow

direct

comparison

of

KL

clustering

across

different

genetic

backgrounds.

Therefore,

it

remains

unconfirmed

whether

FT-IR

typing

by

KL

would

always

distinguish

unrelated

STs

with

the

same

KL

and

future

studies

are

needed

to

address

these

complementary

genomic

approaches.

Furthermore,

we

created

a

classifier

using

54

isolates

correctly

separated

by

the

KL,

in

order

to

classify

the

remaining

isolates.

When

was

performed,

15

their

KL,

whereas

only

77

with

KL15,

KL10

and

KL46

(not

included

in

the

classifier

training

set)

wrongly

as

KL

102.

Nevertheless,

the

score

of

-

the

confidence

value

(0–100%)

classifier

when

KL

type

-

was

0%

(Table

1),

which

as

expected.

Interestingly,

1

isolate

(GKPN

0375),

which

was

correctly

classified

into

its

KL,

showed

a

0%

score,

indicating

the

classifier

may

be

improved,

possibly

considering

different

or

different

parameters

for

accepting

the

results

of

the

classifier.

Therefore,

more

studies

are

needed

before

considering

the

classifier

for

use

in

a

laboratory

routine.

To

the

best

of

our

knowledge,

this

is

the

first

to

use

the

KL

to

type

different

strains

of

K.

pneumoniae

IR

Biotyper

technology.

Use

of

a

classifier

considering

the

KLs

and

STs

in

IR

Biotyper

a

pneumoniae

in

a

faster

and

compared

WGS.

condition

iron

restriction

in

vitro
,

antimicrobial

susceptibility

testing

by

broth

microdilution

reference

method

iron

to

reliable

technical

issues.

In

contrast

to

its

high

clinical

potential,

the

AST

of

this

antimicrobial

has

been

a

challenge

for

microbiology

laboratories.

In

fact,

EUCAST

established

that

the

disk

diffusion

for

presents

whether

ATU.

laboratories

zone

results

DD

within

ATU

by

a

reference

method

BMD.

laboratory

not

to

test

by

BMD,

results

of

DD

within

should

according

the

zone

diameter

in

the

breakpoint

table

[5].

Conversely,

our

study

showed

that

the

majority

of

presente

estudo

a

prevalência

em

no

um

dos

de

alta

complexidade

da

região

Sul

do

Brasil,

ao

longo

de

um

período

de

um

ano

(2023).

Esses

achados

contribuem

de

forma

significativa

para

o

entendimento

do

cenário

local

de

resistência

aos

carbapenêmicos

em

um

centro

de

referência,

a

importância

da

vigilância

microbiológica

contínua.

Adicionalmente,

foi

possível

estabelecer

o

perfil

de

suscetibilidade

desses

isolados

frente

a

novos

antimicrobianos

-

cefiderocol,

meropenem–vaborbactam

e

sulbactam–durlobactam

-

ainda

não

disponíveis

para

uso

clínico

no

Brasil.

A

avaliação

da

atividade

in

vitro

desses

agentes

fornece

subsídios

relevantes

para

o

conhecimento

epidemiológico

e

terapêutico,

especialmente

no

contexto

de

uma

futura

incorporação

dessas

opções

no

arsenal

antimicrobiano

nacional.

Paralelamente,

avaliou-se

o

perfil

de

suscetibilidade

in

vitro

à

ceftazidima–avibactam,

antimicrobiano

recentemente

introduzido

na

prática

clínica

brasileira,

ampliando

a

compreensão

sobre

sua

efetividade

frente

a

isolados

multirresistentes.

O

estudo

também

permitiu

a

identificação

de

achados

epidemiológicos

relevantes,

incluindo

o

aumento

da

prevalência

da

enzima

NDM

em

isolados

de

Pseudomonas

aeruginosa

e

a

caracterização

de

um

surto

envolvendo

Acinetobacter

seifertii

pertencente

a

uma

nova

cepa

durante

o

período

avaliado.

Esses

resultados

evidenciam

a

dinâmica

evolutiva

dos

mecanismos

de

resistência

e

ressaltam

o

impacto

clínico

e

epidemiológico

de

clones

emergentes

em

ambientes

hospitalares.

No

que

tange

a

comparação

entre

os

métodos

de

disco-difusão

e

microdiluição

em

caldo

para

a

determinação

da

suscetibilidade

ao

cefiderocol,

foi

possível

determinar

discrepâncias

significativas

entre

as

técnicas.

Esses

achados

reforçam

a

necessidade

de

cautela

por

parte

dos

laboratórios

de

microbiologia

clínica

na

interpretação

dos

resultados

obtidos

por

disco-difusão,

bem

como

97

sugerem

a

importância

de

revisões

críticas

dos

pontos

de

corte

clínicos

atualmente

recomendados

por

diretrizes

internacionais,

como

o

EUCAST,

esse

antimicrobiano.

fim,

a

avaliação

do

equipamento

IR

Biotyper,

desenvolvimento

de

um

classificador

a

tipagem

de

,

clonal

científico

de

epidemiologia
